validation_reason: Oracle reproduced the vulnerability and detected the maintainer fix.

vulnerable.evidence: Object.prototype.polluted_marker_1794488918220 was set to true via defaultsDeep({constructor:{prototype:{...}}}) payload; new plain objects now inherit it

fixed.evidence: defaultsDeep call with malicious payload completed without throwing, and Object.prototype.polluted_marker_1794488927102 remains undefined; prototype pollution did not occur

oracle.explanation: The oracle loads lodash from /consumer's node_modules and first performs a benign defaultsDeep merge of two plain objects to confirm the API functions correctly (setting operation_completed=true only after this succeeds). It then attempts the classic CVE-2019-10744 prototype pollution payload `{constructor:{prototype:{<marker>:true}}}` passed as a source to defaultsDeep against an empty target object. After the call, it checks whether Object.prototype now has the unique marker property (both directly and via a freshly created plain object), which indicates successful prototype pollution (exploit_succeeded=true) on vulnerable lodash 4.17.11. On the patched version (4.17.12+), defaultsDeep no longer propagates the constructor/prototype keys, so Object.prototype remains unpolluted regardless of whether the call throws or silently no-ops, yielding exploit_succeeded=false while operation_completed stays true since the benign call already succeeded. Any failure during setup, module resolution, or the benign call is reported as operation_completed=false, and the global pollution is cleaned up afterward to avoid cross-test contamination. No Git, filesystem writes, or network/process operations are used.
